images.alt: Front view of a Sony NWS-3710 RISC workstation: a beige desktop tower with a hinged front cover, power button and status lights
images.caption: A Sony NWS-3710 — a desktop RISC workstation from Sony's NEWS (Network Engineering WorkStation) line, the same MIPS-based family as this station's portable NWS-3260. No NWS-3260 photograph exists on Commons, so its stablemate stands in for it.
images.author: SupremeDalek

images.alt: The front of a Sony NWS-3710 with its cover tilted down, exposing an empty 5.25-inch drive bay, a floppy drive, a configuration DIP switch and a reset button
images.caption: The front panel opened up: floppy drive, the configuration DIP switches and a reset button. It is a DIP switch just like these — set for Automatic Boot — that brings NEWS-OS up unattended on the NWS-3260 emulated here.
images.author: SupremeDalek

images.alt: Rear view of a Sony NWS-3710 workstation showing three expansion bays, one holding a video card, and the rear connector panel
images.caption: The back of the machine: three expansion bays and the connector panel of a late-1980s Japanese Unix workstation. Sony's NEWS line ran a BSD-derived Unix, the ancestor of the NEWS-OS 4.1R booting on this station.
images.author: SupremeDalek

images.alt: Top view of a Sony NEWS UNIX workstation with the upper cover removed, showing the internal boards, drives and power supply
images.caption: Inside, cover removed — the boards, drives and single cooling fan of a NEWS workstation. The NWS-3260 packed this same MIPS R3000A architecture into a portable, LCD-equipped chassis instead of a desktop box.
images.author: SupremeDalek

images.alt: A video card removed from a Sony NEWS 3710 workstation, held up to show the components on the board
images.caption: The graphics board lifted out of the machine. On the NWS-3260 the equivalent display hardware drove a built-in 1120x780 monochrome LCD — the framebuffer this station captures directly.
images.author: SupremeDalek
